subject: Clarification: which hosting variants are included in penetration testing (tenant/data-plane boundaries)
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@acme-corp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: penetration test report and scope clarification for Acme POC

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Our InfoSec team is preparing a short checklist before we spin up the POC and they asked for your recent penetration test report plus a short note clarifying which hosting configurations were covered. Specifically they want to know:

- Were Dedicated (reserved) GPU pools included, or only the multi-tenant Hosted API?
- For Private/VPC deployments, is the customer data-plane (model datastore, KMS endpoints) considered in-scope or out-of-scope for Redwood's PT?
- Any known limitations (e.g., no external network testing for on-prem packages)?

Can you share the report (or an executive summary) and a one-page boundary diagram that we can attach to the Acme security review? If there are any environment labels or build tags we should reference when we provision the POC, please include them.

Appreciate a quick turn — our security review is scheduled for the week of Nov 29.

Thanks,
Lena Park
Security Program Manager
Acme Corp

[External Attachment: acme-security-request-REQ-4591.pdf]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report and scope clarification for Acme POC

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and attaching a diagram.

- Hosted API (multi-tenant): included in our external penetration tests. Report attached (PII redacted).
- Dedicated (reserved pools): included where the environment was managed by Redwood (i.e., Redwood Dedicated running in our cloud accounts). Note: Dedicated with customer-managed infrastructure (if any) may have reduced coverage; see details below.
- Private / VPC (private control plane + customer-managed compute): typically our standard tests cover the Redwood-managed control plane and any managed data paths. Customer-managed components (on-prem compute, customer VPC network, customer KMS) are out-of-scope unless explicitly contracted and instrumented for testing.
- On-prem package (air-gapped): we do not perform external network testing against customer air-gapped environments by default; we supply a remediation checklist and on-site engagement options.

I'm attaching: the redacted PT report, and a tenant/data-plane boundary diagram. Karthik (security) and Marissa (Customer Success) are looped in; Karthik will add technical boundary language we typically provide in attestation letters.

Next steps: please confirm which hosting variant you'll use for the POC (Hosted, Dedicated (Redwood-managed), or Private/VPC with customer-managed compute). If you select Private/VPC and want Redwood to include the customer compute in scope, we'll need a Statement of Work (SOW) addendum to provide agent access and run the tests.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: penetration test report and scope clarification for Acme POC

Hi Lena — adding the technical boundary language for Acme's review. Feel free to paste into your intake doc.

Executive summary of scope delineation (Redwood PTs):

- Redwood-hosted (multi-tenant) API endpoints: in-scope. Tests include authentication flows, API endpoint fuzzing, input sanitization checks, rate-limiting, privilege escalation attempts, and container escape checks on the Redwood-managed runtime.

- Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed): in-scope when the Dedicated cluster is deployed in Redwood's cloud accounts under Redwood management. This includes the serving runtime, autoscaling control plane, and managed datastore snapshots. If the Dedicated cluster is deployed into a customer-managed cloud account (customer retains control plane credentials), the portion of the deployment that is customer-managed is out-of-scope unless covered by an SOW.

- Private / VPC: split responsibilities. Our standard tests cover the Redwood control plane (management APIs, orchestration components) and any network egress points we manage. Components that reside inside the customer's VPC (compute instances running model serving, customer-managed KMS, private data stores) are considered out-of-scope unless we are granted scoped penetration testing access (e.g., on-boarding of a temporary test agent, bastion, or signed access).

- On-prem / air-gapped: out-of-scope for external black-box testing. We offer an on-site testing engagement (scoped separately) and provide a remediation checklist and hardened deployment guide.

Notes / limitations:
- We do not perform social-engineering tests of customer staff.
- Tokenization/PII in reports is redacted; full technical artifacts can be shared under an NDA or supported SOC2 plus SIG process.
- If Acme requires coverage of customer-managed compute/KMS, we will need: (1) a list of hosts and IP ranges, (2) temporary test credentials, and (3) a signed SOW amendment. Typical lead time is 2–3 weeks for scheduling the testing window.

If you confirm the POC variant, Marissa will coordinate the SOW/ops steps and timeline.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
